answer:
Main computation complete and approved approach executed end-to-end. Results:

PC1 (standardised fit, sign fixed so loadings sum > 0) explains 30.3% of total variance (top-3 PCs: 62.7%). Loadings on all 12 variables: ZCU_AU +0.407 (social), Zkeverz +0.382 (cultural), ZKeform -0.353 (cultural), ZHort +0.340 (economic), ZAxtSchwert +0.299 (symbolic), ZDolch +0.266 (symbolic), ZBeil -0.242 (economic), ZMW +0.242 (economic), Zamber -0.239 (social), Zhausgr +0.225 (symbolic), ZMonument +0.204 (social), ZSichel -0.149 (economic). PC1 is a balanced composite of all four capital dimensions rather than a single-dimension axis; its positive pole is copper/gold, pottery decoration, depots and weapons, its negative pole pottery form, axes/celts and amber.

Phase characterisation (PC1 scores, chronological order):
- Middle Neolithic 3400→3000 BCE: -0.583, -1.280, -1.757, -1.467, -1.783. Net FALLING trajectory, first-to-last change -1.199 (≈ -1.2 SD), mean -1.374, with a transient rebound at 3100 BCE.
- Younger Neolithic 2900→2300 BCE: -1.504, -1.599, -0.683, -1.116, -1.214, -1.293, -0.412. Net RISING trajectory, first-to-last change +1.092 (≈ +1.1 SD), mean -1.117; non-monotonic (early dip 2900→2800, mid rebound at 2700, secondary dip to 2400, sharp rise at 2300 BCE).

Hypothesis: the composite first principal component of capital declines across the Middle Neolithic (from -0.58 at 3400 BCE to -1.78 at 3000 BCE, Δ ≈ -1.2 standard deviations) and then recovers across the Younger Neolithic (from -1.50 at 2900 BCE to -0.41 at 2300 BCE, Δ ≈ +1.1 SD), so that by 2300 BCE the capital composite has returned to roughly the level it had at the start of the Middle Neolithic. The decline/rebound is a whole-composite phenomenon: positive-loadings variables (copper/gold, pottery decoration, depots, hatchets/swords, daggers) fall in the MN and rise in the YN, while negative-loadings variables (pottery form, axes/celts, amber) move in the opposite direction.

Robustness: PCA on the raw (unre-standardised) values gives EVR 0.318 and PC1 scores correlating 0.997 with the standardised fit (same loadings, same phase pattern). Cross-check: independently binning the annual time_series_data.csv (raw series, 100-y means, 37 bins 500–4100 BCE) gives PC1 EVR 0.324 with the same directional pattern — MN Δ = -1.17, YN Δ = +1.04, and the same bin-by-bin shape (MN: -0.87, -1.47, -2.24, -1.66, -2.04; YN: -1.72, -1.85, -1.13, -1.34, -1.39, -1.44, -0.68).

payload.hypothesis: In a PCA of the 12 forms-of-capital indicators analysed in 100-year slices (PC1, ~30% of variance, a balanced composite of all four capital dimensions with strongest positive loadings on copper/gold, pottery decoration, depots and weapons and negative loadings on pottery form, axes/celts and amber), the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) is characterised by a net decline in PC1 (from -0.58 to -1.78, about -1.2 standard deviations, with a brief rebound around 3100 BCE), while the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) is characterised by a net recovery (from -1.50 to -0.41, about +1.1 SD, dip in the early/mid phase and a sharp rise at 2300 BCE), returning the capital composite to roughly its 3400 BCE level by the end of the Younger Neolithic.
payload.workflow: Parsed capital.csv (decimal commas to float; dropped group/color); global z-score standardisation (ddof=1) of the 12 Z-variables across all 39 100-year bins; SVD-based PCA with PC1 sign fixed so loadings sum positive; extracted per-bin PC1 scores, loadings and explained variance; robustness check via PCA on raw values (corr 0.997); cross-check by independently binning the annual time_series_data.csv into 100-year means and repeating the PCA (same directional pattern).
